title: Routine consistency
content: Keep feeding, walks, litter care, and other regular care tasks on a predictable schedule when practical. When a routine changes, make a small, observable adjustment and note how the pet responds. An established veterinarian care plan takes priority over a general planning suggestion.

title: Medication safety
content: Use medications only as directed by the pet's veterinarian. A planner can remind an owner about a prescribed task, but it must not recommend a dosage, a substitute medication, or a change to a treatment plan. Contact the prescribing veterinarian when a dose is missed or a medication question is urgent.

title: Enrichment and observation
content: Choose enrichment and activity that match the pet's species, age, mobility, and observed comfort. Introduce unfamiliar activities gradually, supervise when appropriate, and stop an activity if the pet appears distressed.

title: Urgent veterinary help
content: Signs such as trouble breathing, collapse, seizures, uncontrolled bleeding, suspected poisoning, or severe distress need prompt professional veterinary help. A scheduling assistant cannot diagnose an emergency or replace a veterinarian.
